requirements.statement: The service has a Manage templates page, with the page title 'Manage templates - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the H1 'Manage templates'; its path follows the real service's conventions.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives users one place to find, use and create notification templates; no real service has templates today.

requirements.statement: Under the Manage templates heading the page shows the line 'Select, manage or create new notification templates'.
requirements.why: The design's introductory copy for the templates list.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has a primary 'Create new template' button (a link styled as a button) that starts a new template.
requirements.why: The design's way into creating a template.

requirements.statement: Every templates page (Manage templates, Enter template name, the template page, and the delete and discard confirmations) shows the Alpha phase banner 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', the feedback link going to the service's real feedback address rather than the prototype's '#'.
requirements.why: The design shows the phase banner on every templates page; the prototype's dead '#' link is a placeholder.

requirements.statement: On every templates page the service navigation marks 'Templates' as the active item.
requirements.why: Templates is a top-level area of the service in the design, beside the dashboard and address book.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has no Back link: it starts directly with its heading.
requirements.why: It is a top-level page reached from the service navigation or the dashboard.

requirements.statement: The templates are listed under an H2 'My templates'.
requirements.why: The design's heading for the list.

requirements.statement: Above the template cards a results count reads 'Show 1-N of N results' for N templates, or 'Show 0 of 0 results' with none; every template is listed on one page with no pagination control.
requirements.why: The design's results count; it shows no paging.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has a 'Sort by:' select with the options 'Select one' (empty value), 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', preselecting the option that matches the current sort, outside any form and with no apply button; as in Design Release 2.1, choosing an option does not reorder the list. The select's name is the service's.
requirements.why: The design shows the select and never makes it reorder anything; the prototype wins on look and feel, and neither a DR1 judgement on this list nor a real constraint justifies departing from it (c-185). Field names are not the prototype's to decide (c-templates-001).

requirements.statement: Manage templates has no filter or search, and no empty-state message: with no templates it shows the results count and an empty list.
requirements.why: The design has none of these; the prototype shows only the count when the list is empty.

requirements.statement: The templates list shows the user's saved templates newest saved first, leaving out any template that has been deleted.
requirements.why: The design's list order: a template just saved appears at the top.

requirements.statement: Each template is a card labelled 'Template <title>' that shows the template's category label above the template title, which is an H3.
requirements.why: The design's template card.

requirements.statement: Each template card has a 'View template' link to that template's page and a 'Use template' link that starts a notification from it in the template's own set (live animals or germinal products).
requirements.why: The card's two actions in the design; templates carry their type, so each card links to its own set (ruling 9 October).

requirements.statement: Each template card lists, in this order, Commodity (the commodity common names), Origin (the country of origin), Consignee (the consignee's name) and Consignor (the consignor's name), each reading 'Not applicable' when the template has no answer.
requirements.why: The design summarises a template by these four answers so a user can tell templates apart.

requirements.statement: A template's category label is the set it was created in: 'Live animals' for a live animals template and 'Germinal products' for a germinal products template.
requirements.why: The design labels each template card with its category; each set holds one category and a template carries its type, so the label comes from the type rather than from working out what the goods are (c-templates-009).

requirements.statement: The templates pages render as the design does, built from GOV.UK Frontend components (summary cards for the template card and the answer cards, the standard caption, heading, input, button and button group) where the prototype wraps them in custom app-dr2-* and app-view-template-page blocks.
requirements.why: The prototype's custom blocks are its own scaffolding; the real services stay inside the GOV.UK Frontend toolbox while matching what users see.

requirements.statement: A success message on Manage templates shows as a GOV.UK success notification banner (role alert) titled 'Success' with the message as its heading, shown once; it does not dismiss itself and stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: The design confirms saves and deletions this way; its 5-second auto-dismiss gives way to the accessibility duty (c-006).

requirements.statement: Saving a template shows the banner '<template title> saved to templates' on Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that the template was saved.

requirements.statement: Deleting a template shows the banner '<template title> has been deleted' on Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that the template was deleted.

requirements.statement: Templates are stored by the animals backend and kept between sessions: a user's list holds only templates really saved, with no seeded example templates.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps templates in the browser session with five seeded examples because it cannot persist; persistence is a real constraint that overrides the prototype (c-183, kept by the 9 October ruling). Template mode offers only the types whose service stores templates, live animals and germinal products, both in the animals services.

requirements.statement: A saved template is private to the signed-in user who saved it and is listed under their 'My templates'; nobody else sees, uses, changes or deletes it. How the store keys it is the backend's design.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps saved templates to the user who made them under 'My templates'; real persistence and sign-in only replace its session with a store scoped to that user (c-184). The data shape is not the prototype's to decide.

requirements.statement: Opening a template that does not exist or has been deleted, on its page, its change, use or delete pages, redirects to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design never shows an error page for a missing template.

requirements.statement: 'Create new template' starts a new, empty template and sends the user to the notification type question first; the journey then runs notification type, Enter template name, then the notification questions from Origin of the import. Any draft notification the user already has is left untouched.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the type before the name so the template's questions fit its type. The prototype clears its one in-session journey; real drafts are persisted, so starting a template leaves them alone (c-183).

requirements.statement: In template creation the notification type page asks 'What are you importing?' under the caption 'About the consignment', with radios offering only Live animals and Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos), none preselected, and a 'Continue' button that leads to the template name page; its back link goes to Manage templates and it shows no 'Template' caption yet. Submitting it with no choice shows the page's usual error, whose error summary link goes to the first radio. The field name is the service's.
requirements.why: The design's first step of a new template. Template mode offers only the types whose service stores templates, so the plants types are left out until plants has templates (c-templates-008); the field name is not the prototype's to decide.

requirements.statement: The template name page has the caption 'Create a new template', the H1 'Enter template name' and the page title 'Enter template name - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The design's template name page.

requirements.statement: The template name page has one text input, labelled by the H1 with a visually hidden label 'Enter template name', and no hint. The field name is the service's.
requirements.why: The design's single question on the page.

requirements.statement: The template name is optional and unvalidated: the form posts with browser validation off, and a blank name moves on to Origin of the import with no error; there is no length, character or duplicate-name rule.
requirements.why: The design accepts any name, including none.

requirements.statement: A template saved with no name is titled 'Untitled template': the banner reads 'Untitled template saved to templates' and it is listed first with every card field 'Not applicable' when nothing was answered.
requirements.why: The design's fallback name for an unnamed template.

requirements.statement: The template name page has a 'Save and continue' button and a 'Cancel and return to manage templates' link to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's actions on the name page.

requirements.statement: The template name page's back link goes to the notification type page when a type has been chosen, and to Manage templates otherwise.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the name page.

requirements.statement: The template name field is prefilled with the name already entered only while the user is part way through creating that template, and is otherwise empty; a saved template's name cannot be changed afterwards.
requirements.why: The design sets the name only at creation and offers no rename.

requirements.statement: Submitting the template name trims it and opens Origin of the import for the new template, keeping the chosen notification type.
requirements.why: The design's hand-off from the name page into the template's questions.

requirements.statement: A template is answered on the same question pages as a notification, with the same questions, hints and guidance (for example the origin page's country search, region of origin and internal reference, and the commodity page's ITAHC guidance and trade tariff link), each page in template mode showing a 'Template' caption with the template name above the section caption.
requirements.why: The design reuses the notification questions for templates and marks them as a template.

requirements.statement: While a new template is being created, Origin of the import shows the 'Template' caption and name and the caption 'About the consignment', offers only 'Save and continue' (no Cancel link), and its back link returns to the template name page.
requirements.why: The design's first question page in template creation.

requirements.statement: While a new template is being created, 'What are you importing?' shows the 'Template' caption and name, has a back link to the origin page, and offers 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's commodity page actions in template creation.

requirements.statement: In template mode, saving 'What are you importing?' returns to the template's task list instead of going on to the main import reason.
requirements.why: The design lets the user choose which template sections to fill from the task list.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the status strip on its task list and question pages shows a grey 'Template' tag followed by the template's name, in place of the draft status and notification reference.
requirements.why: The design marks the task list as a template's.

requirements.statement: A template's task list is headed 'Template tasklist' instead of 'Notification tasklist', and keeps the 'Overview' H1 and the 'Your commodities' figures for animals and packages (0 and 0 before any are entered).
requirements.why: The design's template task list heading and overview.

requirements.statement: A template's task list has five sections and no Documents section or 'Upload documents' task: '1. About the consignment', '2. Description of the goods', '3. Transport and arrival', '4. Consignment parties' and '5. Contact address'.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to one consignment, so the design leaves them out of templates.

requirements.statement: A live animals template's tasks are: Where is this consignment coming from?, What are you importing?, Main import reason, Commodity details, Identification details, Additional details, Arrival details, Transport details, Roles and addresses (hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination') and Contact address for this consignment, each linking to its question page.
requirements.why: The design's template task list. No ?from= marker is copied; the pages' return behaviour is the service's (ruling 9 October).

requirements.statement: Each task on a template's task list shows a status tag: green 'Complete' when answered, blue 'To do' otherwise.
requirements.why: The design shows the user which template sections are filled.

requirements.statement: A template's task list ends with a primary 'Review template' button to the template review and a secondary 'Return to manage templates' button to Manage templates, in place of 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: The design's template task list actions.

requirements.statement: A template never offers documents or a declaration: nothing on a template's task list, pages or review leads to Upload documents or the declaration, and the template review's main button saves the template instead. The prototype's redirects that guard the documents, declaration and submitted addresses in template mode are not required.
requirements.why: A template has no documents and no declaration (ruling 9 October); the prototype's URL guards are its own routing and are not required (c-templates-007).

requirements.statement: The template review's back link returns to the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the template review.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the template review's Change links open each question page directly to change the template in progress, not the saved-template change flow (with its 'Save and return' and 'Cancel' back to the template page).
requirements.why: During creation the template is still a draft being reviewed.

requirements.statement: 'Save template' saves the template, even with only some sections answered, and returns to Manage templates with the new template first in the list and the count one higher.
requirements.why: The design lets a user save a partial template.

requirements.statement: Saving a template that is being edited overwrites it, keeping its id, and moves it to the top of the list rather than adding a copy.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling with the unlinked whole-template edit mode (c-templates-004): no page links to that mode, so saving a template being edited through it is not built. A saved template is changed one section at a time (req-1361).

requirements.statement: A new template's id, used in its addresses, is its title in lower case with every run of other characters replaced by a hyphen ('template' if nothing is left), with -2, -3 and on added when the user already has that id.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: template ids built from titles are data-model shape copied from the prototype (c-templates-002). How a template is identified is the backend's design.

requirements.statement: A template's date created is set to the day it is saved, and is reset each time it is saved again after a change.
requirements.why: The design shows this date on the template page and updates it on every save.

requirements.statement: A template saves the notification's country and region of origin, internal reference, commodity codes, common names and species, reason for import, purpose in the market, certified for, unweaned animals, storage temperature, animal and package totals and per-species numbers, commodity selections, net weight, package type, animal identification details, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification, transport document reference, the transporter's name, address, country, approval number and type, and the CPH number.
requirements.why: These are the answers the design carries from one consignment to the next.

requirements.statement: A template never holds an arrival date or time, including after a section of an existing template is changed and saved.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the arrival date out of templates because it differs for every consignment.

requirements.statement: A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, shows them on the template page's Addresses card (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and Contact address card as the design renders them, and seeds each back into a notification started from it; the contact address falls back to the place of origin where none was chosen, as the design does.
requirements.why: The real notification persists the parties separately and sends each downstream as its own party, so the prototype's shortcut of copying the place of origin into every party would name the overseas place of origin as the GB consignee, importer and destination: a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-186).

requirements.statement: A saved template's page has the caption 'Templates' above the template's title, which is its H1 and its page title ('<template name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK').
requirements.why: The design's page for one saved template.

requirements.statement: The template page shows 'Date created: <d Month yyyy>' with the template's date created.
requirements.why: The design shows when the template was last saved.

requirements.statement: The template page has a primary 'Use template' button that starts a notification from the template and a red warning 'Delete' button that opens the template's delete confirmation.
requirements.why: The design's actions on a saved template.

requirements.statement: The template page's back link goes to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from a template.

requirements.statement: The template page has no Edit button or link, and there is no whole-template edit: a saved template is changed one section at a time through its Change links.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows no edit action on the template page, and the 9 October ruling drops its unlinked edit mode (c-templates-004).

requirements.statement: The template page lists the template's answers in the same cards as the notification review, in five numbered sections, '1. About the consignment' (Origin of import, What are you importing?, Main import reason), '2. Description of the goods' (a card per commodity '<common name> (<code>)' with species, Number of animals, Number of packages (when required), the identification details table, and an Additional details card), '3. Transport and arrival' (Arrival details and Transport details), '4. Consignment addresses' and '5. Contact address', with no documents section and a Change link on every card.
requirements.why: The design lets the user check everything a template holds before using it.

requirements.statement: On the template page each card's Change link changes that section of the saved template: origin of the import, what you are importing, reason for import, consignment details (card header and number-of-animals row), animal identification details, additional animal details, arrival details, transporter, roles and addresses and contact address.
requirements.why: The design changes one section of a saved template at a time.

requirements.statement: A success message on the template page shows as a success banner titled 'Success', shown once and staying until the trader leaves or reloads the page; opening the template page abandons any half-finished change to a template.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation of a change, and its way of leaving an unfinished change; its 5-second auto-dismiss gives way to the accessibility duty (c-006).

requirements.statement: Posting to a template's page (/templates/<id>) changes nothing and redirects back to that page.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: a POST to the template page is the prototype's routing, not look and feel (c-templates-005).

requirements.statement: Following a template's Change link opens that section's question page prefilled from the template, to change the saved template rather than a notification.
requirements.why: The design changes a saved template on the ordinary question pages.

requirements.statement: A Change address for a section that is not one of the template's sections redirects back to the template page.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling (claim 20, 'the section allow-list'; claim 21, template URL guards not required): a Change address for a section the template does not have is routing, not look and feel (c-templates-006). The template page only links to the sections it shows.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section from its page or review, each journey page's only submit button is 'Save and return', beside a 'Cancel' link back to that template's page; this ending takes precedence over the amend ending.
requirements.why: The design's actions when changing one section of a saved template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section, the question page's back link returns to the template page.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation when changing a template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section, the question page is prefilled with the template's answers and can be edited; an unanswered optional field is empty, 'Not applicable' being only how the template page shows it.
requirements.why: The design edits the template's existing answers.

requirements.statement: Saving a changed template section saves the template, never a draft notification, and returns to the template's page, which shows the new answer and a success banner headed '<template name> has been updated' ('Template has been updated' when the template has no name); this holds for every section, not only the origin section the traces follow.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that a template change was saved.

requirements.statement: Opening /templates/<id>/edit starts a draft seeded from the template in template-creation mode and opens the template's task list.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: no page links to the whole-template edit mode, so it is not built (c-templates-004).

requirements.statement: Using a template creates and saves a new draft notification in the template's own set, seeded from the template, and opens its task list headed 'Notification tasklist' with the status 'Draft' and a new GBN-AG notification reference made the same way as for any new notification. Any other draft the user has is left untouched.
requirements.why: Using a template is the design's quick way to start a notification from saved answers. The prototype clears its one in-session journey; real drafts are persisted, so using a template leaves them alone (c-183). Germinal notifications keep GBN-AG references.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template uses its set's normal notification task list, including '4. Documents' and '5. Consignment parties', ending with 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard'; nothing on it says which template it came from.
requirements.why: Once started, it is an ordinary notification; the design does not show where it came from.

requirements.statement: The overview of a notification started from a template shows the template's animal and package totals under 'Your commodities'.
requirements.why: The template's numbers carry over.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template records the template's id and title, but nothing on its task list says which template it came from.
requirements.why: Dropped by the 9 October ruling: recording the template's id on the notification is data-model shape copied from the prototype, and nothing a user sees depends on it (c-templates-003). req-1364 keeps that the task list does not name the template.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the country of origin, the region of origin ('Yes' with the code when the template has one, 'No' when it does not) and the internal reference (blank when the template has none).
requirements.why: The origin answers carry over.

requirements.statement: Using a template starts the notification in the template's own set, selects the template's commodities and species, and seeds the commodity selections, animal and package numbers per species, net weight, package type and animal identification details it holds.
requirements.why: The goods answers carry over; a template carries its type, so it starts a notification of that type (ruling 9 October).

requirements.statement: Using a live animals template seeds the main reason for import, the purpose in the internal market only when the reason is 'Internal market', 'certified for' when the template's value is a valid option (otherwise 'Further keeping'), and the unweaned animals answer when valid for the species ('No' when the species have unweaned options and the template has none).
requirements.why: The reason and additional details carry over, falling back to valid answers. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement per set; req-templates-001 carries the germinal half.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the CPH number, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference; it leaves the arrival date empty, so Arrival details and Upload documents show 'To do' on the new notification.
requirements.why: The transport answers carry over; the arrival date and documents are new for every consignment.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the transporter's name, address, approval number, type and country into the new notification.
requirements.why: The design saves and shows the transporter's country and, after a template is used, shows the same country again, worked out from the seeded approval number; the real service stores the country as an answer and a private transporter has no approval number, so it carries the saved country across to give the same result (c-187).

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds no documents and starts the notification with no validation errors.
requirements.why: Documents are never part of a template.

requirements.statement: A saved template's delete confirmation has the H1 'Delete this template?' and the page title 'Delete this template? - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The design asks before a template is deleted.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation shows a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the template's title.
requirements.why: The design names the template being deleted.

requirements.statement: Under the summary the delete confirmation says 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: The design's warning copy.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation has a red warning 'Yes, delete' button that posts the deletion and a 'No, cancel' link back to the template page, in a GOV.UK button group.
requirements.why: The design's confirm and cancel actions.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation's back link goes to the template page.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the delete confirmation.

requirements.statement: The delete and discard confirmations use the journey layout, not the dashboard layout.
requirements.why: The design renders the confirmation as a journey page.

requirements.statement: Confirming 'Yes, delete' removes the template and returns to Manage templates with the '<title> has been deleted' banner and one template fewer in the count.
requirements.why: The design's result of deleting a template.

requirements.statement: A template being created can be discarded from its review: a confirmation shows the same 'Delete this template?' page and copy, with the Name row holding the name entered ('this template' when none), a back link and 'No, cancel' link to the template review, and a 'Yes, delete' button that discards it.
requirements.why: The design lets a user throw away a template before saving it.

requirements.statement: The discard page is shown only while a template is being created; otherwise opening it redirects to Manage templates, and posting to it changes nothing and returns to Manage templates.
requirements.why: There is nothing to discard outside template creation.

requirements.statement: Confirming discard throws the template away unsaved and returns to Manage templates, list unchanged, with the banner '<template name> has been deleted', or 'Template has been deleted' when no name was entered.
requirements.why: The design's result of discarding a template.

requirements.statement: The prototype's /design-release-2.1 mount and its rule sending anyone not in a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session to the start page are not built; the real services serve the templates pages at their own paths behind their own sign-in.
requirements.why: Version mounting and design-release sessions are prototype mechanics, not part of the design.

requirements.statement: The 'Cancel' link on a template's change page pointing to /templates/<id> without the release prefix is not reproduced; Cancel goes to the template page.
requirements.why: A prototype path slip, not part of the design; req-1358 builds the working Cancel link.

requirements.statement: The prototype's unguarded discard post, which clears any notification in progress and shows a 'has been deleted' banner even when no template is being created, is not reproduced.
requirements.why: A prototype defect, not part of the design; req-1381 guards the post.

requirements.statement: The seeded Arena Aintree region code changing from 'ROI-092032' to 'IE-092032' on re-save is not a templates behaviour to build: it comes from seeded data no real service holds.
requirements.why: Seeded templates are not built (c-183); the region code form belongs to the origin page.

requirements.statement: The prototype's session-only storage and its five seeded templates (Arena Aintree, Rice Lane City Farm, Monk Park Farm, Acorn Farm and Glen Keen Farm, with their answers and the '15 April 2026' fallback date) are not built.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (c-183): real users see only templates they saved.

requirements.statement: Saving a template by a GET to /templates/save is not built: a template is saved only by the 'Save template' form post from the review page.
requirements.why: A state-changing GET bypasses the services' request forgery protection, a real constraint the prototype cannot express (c-188).

requirements.statement: Using a germinal products template seeds the main reason for import, the purpose in the internal market only when the reason is 'Internal market', and the storage temperature only when it is one of the germinal products temperature options; 'certified for' is the germinal set's fixed 'Germinal products', and nothing about unweaned animals is asked or seeded.
requirements.why: The germinal half of the template seeding rule, split into its own requirement by the 9 October ruling so it is built in the germinal set; the germinal set sets 'certified for' when the draft is created and always asks for temperature.

requirements.statement: A germinal products template is answered on the germinal set's question pages, so its task list has no Additional details task and it asks no CPH number or permanent address; it is saved, listed with the category 'Germinal products', viewed, changed and deleted like any template, and 'Use template' starts a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: Template mode offers germinal products because its service stores templates, and a template carries its type; the germinal set leaves out Additional details, the CPH number and the permanent address (ruling 9 October). Design Release 2.1 does not show a germinal template, so the germinal set's own pages decide what it asks.

conflicts.about: Where templates live: the prototype's session with five seeded templates, or real persistence.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype default.
Templates and deletions are held only in the user's session.
The service seeds five templates dated 15 April 2026.
Arena Aintree's card and answers.
Arena Aintree's answers in full.
Arena Aintree's movement details.
Shared values of every seeded template.
Rice Lane City Farm's card and answers.
Monk Park Farm's card and answers.
Acorn Farm's card and answers.
Glen Keen Farm's card and answers.
Seeded templates other than Arena Aintree have no contact or transport details.
Deleting a saved template that shares a seeded id brings the seeded one back.
A new template named like a deleted seeded one is saved but never listed.
The template page falls back to 'Date created: 15 April 2026' when a template has no date.
The templates journey makes no calls to other systems; templates are held in the session.
Five templates are seeded.
The seeded template cards' values.
The five seeded templates appear on the list.
c-183 is kept for a real constraint.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling of 7 October ranks first and names persistence as a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and the 9 October ruling keeps this conflict: templates are stored by the backend and kept between sessions, and a user sees only templates really saved, with no seeded examples. The list order (newest saved first), the count, the card and every page design still stand; only the session storage and the seed data are set aside. The prototype's clearing of its one in-session journey when a template is created or used is session storage too: real drafts are persisted, so creating or using a template leaves the user's other drafts untouched. Test suites may create their own templates through the journey.

conflicts.about: Who a stored template belongs to: the user who saved it, or their whole organisation.

positions.says: Templates have no owner, sharing or organisation scope.
No trace shows whether templates are shared across an organisation or private to their maker.

conflicts.outcome: A saved template is private to the signed-in user who saved it and listed under 'My templates'; nobody else sees, uses, changes or deletes it. The prototype wins by default and already keeps saved templates to the user who made them (held in their own session, never shared between users, under a 'My templates' heading); real persistence and sign-in only replace the session with a store scoped to that user, whose shape is the backend's design, so nothing is left for a person to decide.

conflicts.about: What the templates list's 'Sort by:' select does, given the prototype never reorders and templates hold no arrival date.

positions.says: The sort value only preselects an option; the select is outside any form with no apply button, so sorting is not built.
The list has a 'Sort by:' select with Select one, Newest first, Oldest first and Arrival date.
No trace drives the select, so whether it reorders and how Arrival date applies is not shown.

conflicts.outcome: Build Manage templates' 'Sort by:' select as Design Release 2.1 has it: options 'Select one' (empty value), 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', preselecting the option that matches the current sort, outside any form and with no apply button; the select's name is the service's. As in the prototype, the select does not reorder the list, so 'Arrival date' needs no meaning for templates; making the sort work would depart from the prototype with neither a DR1 judgement on this list nor a real constraint to justify it.

conflicts.about: Whether a template saves each consignment party's address, or only the place of origin copied into every party.

positions.says: A template saves only the place of origin and a contact address, records that the same address is used for every party, and using it copies the place of origin into consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination.
The template page lists Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination, each as a full address.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, including cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype default.
c-186 is kept for a real constraint.

conflicts.outcome: A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, shows them on the template page's Addresses card (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and Contact address card as the design renders them, shows the consignee and consignor names on the template card, and seeds each back into a notification started from it; the contact address falls back to the place of origin where none was chosen, as the design does. The design's single copied address is set aside because the real notification persists and sends each party separately, a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.

conflicts.about: Whether using a template seeds the transporter's country it saves and shows.

positions.says: Using a template seeds the transporter's name, address, approval number and type, but not the country.
A template saves the transporter's country.
The template page's Transport details card shows the transporter's Country.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as persistence, overrides the prototype default.

conflicts.outcome: Using a template seeds the transporter's country along with its name, address, approval number and type. The prototype's design saves and shows the country and, after a template is used, shows the same country again (worked out from the seeded approval number); the real service stores the country as an answer and has no approval number for a private transporter, so it carries the saved country into the new notification to give the same result.

conflicts.about: Saving a template by visiting /templates/save with a GET.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default.
A GET to /templates/save saves the template in progress, the same as Save template.
Visiting /templates/save during template creation saves the template.
GET /templates/save redirects and the suite reaches it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a GET that saves bypasses the real services' request forgery protection, a constraint the prototype cannot express. A template is saved only by the 'Save template' form post from the review page, which still produces the same banner and list.

conflicts.about: Whether the templates pages take the prototype's /templates/... paths, ?from= markers and form field names.

positions.says: Templates pages are named by page and section, never by /templates/... paths or ?from= markers.
The prototype never decides URL paths, query parameter or form field names.
The templates list is served at /templates.
A template's Change link redirects to the question page with ?from=template-review.
The template task list's tasks link to their question pages with ?from=hub.
The template name input is named templateName.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first: the templates pages, their content and their destinations are built as Design Release 2.1 shows them, but their paths follow the real service's conventions, no ?from= marker is copied, and query and form field names (the sort select, the template name input, the notification type radios) are the service's. Acceptance criteria assert pages, headings and destinations, not literal paths. No claim is overruled: each prototype claim here still backs the page, link or field it describes; only its path, marker or name is set aside.

conflicts.about: Whether a template's id is built from its title, as the prototype does.

positions.says: req-1342 and inc-157 (template ids built from titles) are dropped.
A new template's id is its title in lower case with other characters hyphenated, with -2, -3 added when taken.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: how a template is identified is data-model shape, the backend's to design. req-1342 is out of scope.

conflicts.about: Whether a notification started from a template records the template's id and title.

positions.says: req-1366 and inc-160 (the template's id on the notification) are dropped.
A notification started from a template remembers the template's id and title.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: nothing a user sees depends on the link, so it is not stored. req-1366 is out of scope; req-1364 keeps that nothing on the task list names the template.

conflicts.about: Whether the prototype's unlinked whole-template edit mode is built.

positions.says: inc-163, req-1341 and req-1362 (the unlinked template edit mode) are dropped.
Editing a whole template starts a draft seeded from it in template-creation mode and opens the hub.
A template being edited keeps its existing id when saved.
Edit opens the template on the notification hub with a 'Template' tag and its name.
Editing a template opens it on its own task list.
GET /templates/:templateId/edit redirects.
Editing a saved template opens the template on its own task list.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: no page links to the whole-template edit, so it is not built (req-1341 and req-1362 are out of scope) and the template page has no Edit action (req-1351). A saved template is changed one section at a time (req-1356 to req-1361). The 'Template' tag and name on a template's task list still stand while a template is being created (req-1328), backed by the creation traces.

conflicts.about: Whether a POST to a template's page redirects back to it.

positions.says: req-1355 and inc-158 criterion 8 (a POST on the template page) are dropped.
Posting to /templates/<id> redirects back to the view template page.
A POST to a template page redirects back to it.
A POST to a template's view page redirects back to it.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the POST handler is the prototype's routing, so req-1355 is out of scope.

conflicts.about: Whether a Change address for a section a template does not have redirects back to the template page (the section allow-list).

positions.says: req-1354 and inc-159 criterion 5 (the section allow-list) are dropped.
The prototype's template URL guards are not required.
A change link for a section not in the allowed list redirects back to the view template page.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first and drops the section allow-list, which this area carries as req-1357 (out of scope). The ruling's id 'req-1354' is read by its own description, 'the section allow-list': req-1354 holds the template page's success banner, which is look and feel the same ruling keeps (claim 16) and which req-1361's 'has been updated' banner needs, so req-1354 stands. The template page links only to the sections it shows.

conflicts.about: Whether template mode keeps the prototype's redirects guarding the documents, declaration and submitted addresses.

positions.says: A template never offers documents or a declaration; the prototype's template URL guards are not required.
In a template, opening Upload documents redirects to the template's task list.
In a template, opening the declaration redirects to the review page.
Visiting upload-documents during a template journey redirects to the task list.
Visiting the declaration during a template journey redirects to the review.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a template never offers documents or a declaration (req-1330, req-1334, and the review's Save template), but the prototype's URL redirects that guard those addresses are not required.

conflicts.about: Which notification types template creation offers: every create-journey type, as the prototype shows, or only the types whose service stores templates.

positions.says: Template mode offers only live animals and germinal products, the types whose service stores templates.
The plants types are left out of template mode until plants has templates.
In a new template the type page offers Live animals, Germinal products, Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products.
The radios carry the values live-animals, germinal-products, plants-for-planting, potatoes and wood-products.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October ruling ranks first: template creation's type question offers Live animals and Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos) only, and a germinal choice makes a germinal products template (req-templates-002). This replaces c-007's 'template creation offers the same options as the create one'. The trace's caption, heading, Continue button and the two kept options still stand; its plants options and radio values are set aside, the values because field values are the service's.

conflicts.about: Where a template's category comes from: worked out from its goods, or the set it belongs to.

positions.says: Templates carry their type, and each template card links to its own set.
Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written.
A saved template's category is 'Germinal products' when the notification has only germinal products, and otherwise 'Live animals'.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a template's category is the set it was made in, shown on the card as 'Live animals' or 'Germinal products', and using it starts a notification in that set. The prototype's rule of working the category out from the goods is set aside; the labels a user sees are unchanged.
